item.title: Sam Smith & Normani Try Again to Dismiss ‘Dancing With a Stranger’ Copyright Lawsuit: ‘Fatal Defect’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. Today, we're talking about a copyright lawsuit involving Sam Smith and Normani's hit song "Dancing With a Stranger".
[Music transitions to a softer tone]
Host: The song, which reached number 7 on the Billboard Hot 100 chart in 2019, has been accused of stealing its hook from an earlier song called "Dancing With Strangers" by Jordan Vincent. But here's the thing - the court case has been ongoing since 2022, and now Smith and Normani's lawyers are trying to throw out the lawsuit once again.
[Short music break]
Host: The lawyers have filed a motion to end the copyright claims without a trial, arguing that there's no evidence to prove that Smith and Normani copied Vincent's song. In fact, Vincent has conceded that there's no proof that the songwriting team ever even heard "Dancing With Strangers".
[Music transitions to a more upbeat tone]
Host: To win the case, Vincent would need to prove that the two songs are "strikingly similar" - nearly identical to a degree that copying is the only logical explanation. But Smith and Normani's lawyers say that's just not the case. They point out that the phrase "dancing with a stranger" has been used in over 15 other songs before Vincent's, including a 1989 Cyndi Lauper song and a 1997 Regina track.
[Music breaks for a brief moment]
Host: And in a surprising twist, Smith and Normani's lawyers have discovered that Vincent's song actually sampled two earlier tracks without licenses, which could render Vincent's copyright invalid.
[Music transitions to a softer tone]
Host: Vincent's lawyer is fighting back, arguing that there's enough evidence to justify a jury trial. But it's clear that this case is getting more complicated by the minute. We'll be keeping an eye on it to see what happens next.
[Outro music plays]
Host: Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more updates on the latest music news and trends.
